summary: DHCP option 121 (classless routes) from build VLAN causes AAD join timeouts and SCCM check-in failures during imaging
summary_full: Multiple workstation provisioning jobs in the US-East build fleet started failing AAD join and SCCM check-in steps after a DHCP configuration change on the build VLAN. Root cause traced to DHCP option 121 (classless static routes) being injected by the new DHCP relay implementation which caused VMs and imaging hosts to learn an incorrect next-hop for the corp DNS and AAD endpoints.
description: Issue summary: Starting 2026-03-10 02:30 UTC, autopilot/SCCM driven provisioning runs in the us-east build pool began failing at the 'Join AzureAD' step and subsequently failed SCCM check-in with error 0x800705B4 (timeout). Impact: ~18% of provisioning jobs in the affected pool failed, blocking depot repairs and delaying laptop returns. Environment: prod build VLAN (vlan-220) behind DHCP relay 10.12.8.5; imaging hosts run the standard Windows 11 task sequence with corporate network bootstrap. Observed: devices get an IP and can reach the DHCP server but appear to resolve AAD endpoints to wrong subnet due to classless static route injection. Expected: no classless static routes from DHCP; default gateway should route to corp firewall for AAD/DNS traffic.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Boot a target device into the imaging task sequence in vlan-220. 2) Allow network boot/WinPE to obtain DHCP lease from relay 10.12.8.5. 3) Start the OOBE/AAD join step or trigger SCCM client registration. 4) Observe DNS/AAD endpoints failing to be reached and the client timing out. 5) Capture ipconfig /all and route print to inspect client routes.
logs:
- ipconfig /all from affected host shows lease from 10.12.8.1 and DHCP options including Option121 with classless static route: 10.0.0.0/8 via 192.168.254.1
- route print shows an erroneous host route that prefers 192.168.254.1 for corp AAD subnets (13.107.0.0/16)
- SCCM logs: Client registration timeout 0x800705B4; Network Access Manager indicates DNS lookup to login.microsoftonline.com failed after 4s retries
- DHCP server logs (relay): relay forwarded option 121 from provisioning-router-sw1 (config change applied 2026-03-10 01:50 UTC)
- tcpdump from imaging host: SYNs to 13.107.x.x are routed to 192.168.254.1 and dropped (no ARP)
investigation_notes:
- 03/10 04:00 UTC: On-call SRE (Diego) confirmed correlation between timing of build VLAN router firmware upgrade and start of failures.
- 03/10 05:10 UTC: Collected ipconfig /all and routing table from 12 affected hosts; consistent Option121 present.
- 03/10 05:40 UTC: Packet captures show DNS queries leaving on incorrect interface; imaging host ARP for 192.168.254.1 times out.
- Hypothesis: Relay/router firmware change started including classless static routes in DHCP offered options; Windows client honors Option121 and installs host routes, outrouting traffic meant for corporate firewall.
- Verified by reproducing on a lab imaging host by injecting Option121 using isc-dhcp-server; host gained route and AAD join timed out.
- Cross-reference: Slack #internal-provisioning thread (https://redwood.slack.com/archives/C0PROV123/p1678512000000) and router firmware PR (fw-team/commit/8af3b2)
comments: Maya Patel (2026-03-10): First noticed imaging failures after morning depot run. CC'ing network and SRE.
Diego Alvarez (2026-03-10): Collected captures and routing tables; suspect DHCP option 121. Opening coordination with firmware team.
Liu Chen (Network, 2026-03-10): Router fw 1.14.2 added feature to push classless routes via relay; rolling back on vlan-220 now.
Diego Alvarez (2026-03-10): Temporarily removed DHCP relay option121 injection; provisioning success rate returned to baseline (99%).
Operations (2026-03-11): Created firewall ACL to block 192.168.254.0/24 from build pool until full fix is applied.
root_cause: A recent router firmware change on the build VLAN's DHCP relay began injecting DHCP option 121 (classless static routes). Windows imaging clients honor Option121, which installed routes that redirected traffic for AAD/DNS to an isolated management subnet with no ARP resolution. This caused AAD join and SCCM registration attempts to time out.
resolution:
- Rolled back router firmware change on vlan-220 (10.12.8.0/24) to stop advertising Option121 (2026-03-10 06:05 UTC).
- Redeployed imaging hosts that had been affected; those reprovisioned successfully.
- Added a temporary DHCP policy on relay to explicitly strip Option121 for build VLANs.
- Applied firewall ACLs to block accidental routing to management subnet from build pool while we validate.
- Patched the router firmware (fw-team/commit/9b7ef3) to make Option121 injection opt-in per VLAN and added an ACL to protect management subnet.
rollout_notes:
- 2026-03-10 06:05 UTC: rollback applied to vlan-220 router.
- 2026-03-10 07:00 UTC: provisioning success rates returned to normal.
- 2026-03-11: firmware patch tested in staging and scheduled for controlled rollout to other fabric routers with opt-in disabled for build VLANs.
- Communicated to depot ops to hold large batches until 2026-03-12 10:00 UTC for additional verification.
follow_up_actions: Network: Add unit test to preflight firmware changes validating DHCP options do not include classless routes for provisioning VLANs.
SRE/Provisioning: Harden imaging task sequence to detect and warn on unexpected host routes prior to AAD join step.
Security: Review ACLs to ensure management subnets are unreachable from build pools by default.
Docs: Add troubleshooting playbook entry in Confluence (Confluence: /confluence/display/PROV/DHCP-Option121-Investigation)
